questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to help other drivers see you. Bright colors with reflective materials make you more visible.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals and brake light. Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Make sure you have enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a motorcycle you don't know?

options.text: Assume it is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride as usual since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Get to know the bike before you ride. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn where the gears are located.

questions.question: What should you do with shoelaces while riding?
questions.explanation: Tuck shoelaces in securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information about your motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate your bike and how to maintain it.

questions.question: What is the best way to survive an accident?

options.text: Ask others how to ride safely.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride one hour after drinking one drink?

options.text: Yes, your skills will not be affected.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.
No, alcohol may still affect your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, alcohol may still affect your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time varies for different people. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can build up in your system even if you drink slowly. Your ability to ride safely can still be impaired.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, face protection is not legally required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is recommended.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you faster, which creates more danger.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Can slow you down using engine power.
Should not be done if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can slow you down using engine power.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting smoothly can help slow your motorcycle. If you use engine braking, activate your brake lights separately to alert other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: To protect yourself while riding, pants should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Be made of a heavy material.
Fit loosely enough to flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of a heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or heavy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: If you wait one hour to ride after having one drink:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even if you drink slowly. This can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should continually scan the road ahead for:
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers in the road are all slippery. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller.
Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals to alert others to your intentions. Use them any time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many conflicts can happen between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots so small they do not cause problems.
Have blind spots that you need to check by turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you need to check by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is that:

options.text: The motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will continue to ride well if it is properly maintained through regular inspection and maintenance.
